_comment: SPEC-APP.md §7.5-§7.6 behavior-training dataset builder config. seed controls every deterministic sampling step (distractor selection, abstention context selection) — the same seed against the same chunks.jsonl/qa-pairs.jsonl always reproduces byte-identical output.

distractor._comment: §7.5a — K distractor chunks bundled alongside the relevant one per accepted pair.

abstention._comment: §7.5b — context chunks are sampled from chunks topically unrelated to the question's source chunk (no shared tag, not linked). messageTemplate/escalationText are the structured-abstention target's answer + judge-escalation pointer (same #ask-a-judge contract `rules ask` uses).
abstention.messageTemplate: The retrieved sources don't clearly settle this — I don't want to guess.
abstention.escalationText: If you need a ruling, ask a judge in #ask-a-judge: https://discord.com/channels/874145774135558164/1020649907314495528

ood._comment: §7.5c — every template in config/ood-templates.json becomes one example; minCount is a floor on the bank's total size, enforced loudly (AbstentionBench lesson: phrasing breadth matters more than volume).
ood.refusalTemplate: I'm built to answer Flesh & Blood questions only — rules, cards, decks, and lore. I can't help with that, but I'm glad to help with anything FAB-related.

dpo._comment: §7.6 — chosen = a hedge prefix (rotated round-robin across pairs) applied to the accepted answer; rejected = a real teacher-rejected answer when APP-012 provides one for the same question, else a rule-based synthetic degradation (citation stripped, or an overconfident-framing prefix applied) rotated round-robin across the two synthetic subtypes.

degradation.confidentWrongPrefix: Definitely — no exceptions, no need to check further:
